segments.title: Chương 141: Tay không bắt cướp
segments.content:
Chapter 144: 0141 Snagging a White Wolf with Bare Hands

The siege on QQ had actually started last year.

NetEase Popo and MSN were the first to make a move, then the Chinese version of Yahoo! Messenger went online, followed by Sina acquiring Longma UC, China Telecom launching VIM, Sohu launching SouQ, 263 launching E-huatong, China Netcom launching Tiantian Instant Messenger, and Ali launching TradeManager…

This was just a partial list of the recognizable names; over 200 products similar to QQ had appeared nationwide!

Just as Tencent's senior management was tearing their hair out, China Mobile stabbed them squarely in the back.

QQ had always been a money loser with worrying profitability, so Tencent could only rely on Mobile Monternet to recoup its losses. The money Tencent earned from Mobile Monternet once accounted for 63.6% of Tencent's total revenue.

Meanwhile, the profit Tencent provided to Mobile Monternet accounted for 24% of Mobile Monternet's total income, with second-place Sina at only 7%. 70% of the SMS messages processed by Monternet came from QQ.

Given this, Tencent and China Mobile should have become close partners.

Like hell they were!

China Mobile was a huge corporation and believed it was the one helping Tencent make money. Moreover, the revenue share in the contract Mobile Monternet had signed with Tencent in the early days was too low: 15% for Monternet, 85% for Tencent (with the actual amount received being 70%).

China Mobile's thinking was: Damn it, Tencent gets seventy percent? Isn't that the same as me kneeling to beg for scraps?

So, at Tencent's critical moment of being besieged, China Mobile hit them while they were down, tossing them a new contract: a 50-50 split!

Although it was called a 50-50 split, after factoring in all the other miscellaneous items, Tencent could get 42% at most.

Tencent was forced to accept the new contract…

When the news got out, Tencent's stock price immediately dropped below its IPO price.

It still hadn't recovered. Tencent was now planning to raise funds to buy back shares in order to boost the stock price and increase investor confidence.

And right at this moment, MSN China was rallying an anti-QQ alliance!

Even then, Tencent had not yet reached its most perilous moment.

In another six months, the Ministry of Information Industry (soon to be the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology) would issue a document to strengthen supervision of mobile information services. That would be the blow that truly hammered Tencent to the brink of death.

Shencheng.

An acquisition contract was being signed.

Zhang Xiaolong was officially selling Foxmail and QQ Mail to Tencent, but he was unwilling to move to Shencheng to work. So Tencent funded the establishment of the Guangzhou R&D Center, with Zhang Xiaolong as its head.

This Zhang Xiaolong was the man who would later create WeChat.

"Pleasure working with you!"

Pony Ma shook hands with Zhang Xiaolong as reporters' cameras flashed.

The first half of the signing ceremony was quite lively and festive.

But when it came to the Q&A session with the reporters at the press conference, Pony Ma found it a bit hard to handle.

"Mr. Ma, there are rumors that MSN is forming an anti-QQ alliance. What countermeasures does Tencent have?" a reporter asked, showing no mercy.

Pony Ma said, "We will continue to work hard on making good products and bringing users a better experience."

Another reporter asked, "Since the '3.15' exposé last year on fraudulent charges in wireless value-added services, complaints have continued to pour in. What corrective measures does Tencent have?"

Pony Ma said, "Tencent is not the only company in the wireless value-added services business. We have the most services, but we receive very few complaints. It's some of our competitors who are damaging the industry ecosystem. Moreover, we are very law-abiding and have actively cooperated with the rectification requirements of the Ministry of Information Industry."

"Tencent's stock price has been below its IPO price since November of last year. What countermeasures does Tencent have?"

"The board of directors has already decided to buy back 10% of the share capital in three installments, plus an additional 60 million US dollars' worth of shares. The buyback plan will be initiated next month. Our transformation has been very successful, and the revenue share from our wireless value-added services is decreasing month by month. This shows that QQ's own profitability is continuously improving…"

The reporters' questions were each more pointed than the last, hitting every one of Tencent's sore spots.

Pony Ma was mentally exhausted. He only stayed for a short while at the luncheon before returning to his office to close his eyes and rest.

Tencent had to transform, and that included changing its corporate structure.

But as for how to transform and how to change, Pony Ma currently had no clear ideas.

"Knock, knock, knock!"

"Come in."

Chief Administrative Officer Charles Chen walked in and sat down opposite Pony Ma. "There's a problem with our management mechanism. The R-line is being dragged down by over 60 product departments, and the progress of all projects is extremely slow. We must connect the R-line and M-line and implement a product manager system. Whoever does well should be allowed to form an independent unit. That's the only way to build combat effectiveness."

"A reform like that will face a lot of resistance," Pony Ma said.

Charles Chen said, "But it must be done. We old-timers will definitely support you."

Pony Ma managed a smile at his words. The resistance to reform came precisely from some of the old-timers.

After stating his position, Charles Chen continued, "There's a company called ByteDance. They contacted our people and said that MSN had invited them to join the anti-QQ alliance. The boss of this company wants to speak with you directly. It's been reported up through the ranks and has reached me."

Pony Ma asked, "What kind of company is ByteDance?"

Charles Chen said, "It was founded by a Peking University student. Its core product is called Xiaonei, which has similar functions to the QQ Zone we're about to launch. But they only focus on campus social networking. In just four months, their user base has grown to over 400,000. And the user growth is accelerating; it's estimated they'll break 1 million in another two months."

"Like Sohu's Alumni Network?" Pony Ma asked.

Charles Chen said, "An evolved, Web 2.0 version of an alumni network. This student is very interesting; he's currently just a freshman."

An idea struck Pony Ma. "How about we acquire Xiaonei?"

Charles Chen shook his head. "Xiaonei's functions overlap with QQ Zone. Besides, Xiaonei called to say that MSN offered 500,000 US dollars for a 20% stake in their company. They flatly rejected the proposal, and MSN is now discussing renegotiating. If MSN is willing to compromise, they might get a 15% or 10% stake in Xiaonei."

"They're overvaluing themselves," Pony Ma commented.

Given Xiaonei's current situation, a valuation of 3 to 4 million US dollars would be more reasonable.

Anything higher, and most venture capitalists would shake their heads.

Because the second wave of the internet investment craze had not yet kicked into high gear in China!

Tencent was very tight on funds right now. They had just acquired the email business, were establishing an R&D center in Guangzhou, and were next going to spend a huge sum on share buybacks.

In addition, Tencent's business was currently bloated and inefficient, and they were thinking about how to reform. It was not a good time to acquire Xiaonei.

"You want me to call him?" Pony Ma asked.

"Yes. I'll send you his number."

Charles Chen added, "I searched online. This kid is also an internet celebrity and a best-selling author. He also started a gaming company that's gaining momentum fast. Some time ago, he publicly criticized *Wolf Totem*, and it got a lot of media attention."

"He's quite the hustler." Pony Ma picked up his phone.

Charles Chen quietly left the office.

The call connected.

"Hello, this is Ma."

"Hello, Mr. Ma. How about you gift me 10 five-digit QQ numbers?"

"Huh?"

Pony Ma was momentarily at a loss for words, not knowing whether to laugh or cry. He thought the other party wanted to discuss some kind of partnership, but instead, he asked for five-digit QQ numbers right off the bat.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm a loyal QQ user, you know. I've loved QQ since I was a kid. MSN's investment offer was so generous, and I still didn't agree… Well, I might eventually agree. Who knows, MSN might even offer a better deal."

"The anti-QQ alliance, right?" Pony Ma asked. "What does MSN want you to do?"

Chen Guiliang said, "That's a confidential business negotiation. I must abide by business ethics before the negotiation concludes. However, including Taobao, nine companies have already joined MSN's anti-QQ alliance."

"I'm already aware of this news," Pony Ma said.

Of course, MSN had released the news in advance to further crush investor confidence and keep Tencent's stock price down.

Chen Guiliang asked, "If I terminate negotiations with MSN, can I make two deals with Tencent?"

"What deals?" Pony Ma asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Help me post two sponsored articles for free on Tencent.com, one to promote my game, *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, and one to promote my novel, *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. For the game channel on Tencent.com, give me a banner ad recommendation spot for five days and a sidebar ad for a month. And please give me a fifty-percent discount on the advertising fees."

"You called me just for this?" Pony Ma was a little speechless.

Chen Guiliang laughed. "It's a small business, I can't afford the advertising fees. I know my own worth right now; I wouldn't dare make an outrageous demand to Mr. Ma. Let's just be friends; perhaps we'll have a chance to cooperate in the future. In return, Xiaonei's ad spots can also give Tencent's products a fifty-percent discount."

What 'in return'? This was purely to drum up business for Xiaonei!

It was about more than just a simple fee. In the future, when Ao Yanchen was negotiating business, he could promote it like this: "The effectiveness of our ads on Xiaonei is excellent. Even Tencent advertises on Xiaonei…"

This would be a great help in expanding Xiaonei's business.

While this was a big deal for Chen Guiliang, it was a trivial matter for Pony Ma.

Pony Ma was actually more interested in those 10 five-digit QQ numbers.

Because high-end business professionals in China, especially the senior management of large corporations, were now exclusively using MSN. Even if you usually used a QQ number, you would be asked to use MSN when contacting other companies.

This trend was now spreading to small and medium-sized companies.

Pony Ma said, "I can give you 10 five-digit QQ numbers. You're an internet celebrity. I hope you will publicly declare on your blog and your Xiaonei homepage that you use QQ for work."

"Sure," Chen Guiliang said. "If the ads on Tencent's game channel for my *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* can be free, and for double the duration I just proposed. I could even write a dedicated blog post enumerating the advantages QQ has over MSN."

This proposal made Pony Ma's eyes light up.

Right, he could ask those well-known bloggers to help post some sponsored articles for QQ.

The two reached a deal and wasted no more words.

Half an hour later, Chen Guiliang received a text message containing 10 QQ numbers and their passwords, as well as the phone number of the person in charge of Tencent.com's advertising department.

Chen Guiliang very happily announced, "In light of the outstanding contributions made by Ao Yanchen, Guo Feng, and Dong Qianqiu to the company, I am now rewarding each of them with a five-digit QQ number. Other employees, as long as you achieve impressive results in the future, will also be rewarded with five-digit QQ numbers!"

Xie Yang had been coveting Chen Guiliang's six-digit QQ number for a long time. He thought to himself that he had been doing a good job, and he was an old classmate, so he would probably be in the next batch of rewards for sure.

Ao Yanchen, however, thought: Why do I feel like something's not right? This reward costs nothing at all. It's snagging a white wolf with bare hands.

(End of Chapter)
